questions: Does the patient have a history of epilepsy or seizures?
Are there any other abnormal movements in the face, neck, or limbs?
Does the patient report dry eyes, irritation, or pain?
Has the patient recently started any new medications, particularly antipsychotics or antiemetics?
Does the blinking worsen with stress or fatigue?
Can the patient voluntarily suppress the blinking for a short period?
orders: Observe the patient performing rapid finger tapping and serial subtraction to assess for distractibility and cognitive load effects on blinking rate
Ask the patient to perform voluntary eye closure and opening at a self-paced rhythm, then attempt to match an externally paced metronome, observing for entrainment or loss of rhythmicity
Examine the eyelids for signs of mechanical restriction, ptosis, or lagophthalmos during attempted full closure
Assess for presence of positive sensory phenomena (premonitory urge) by asking if the patient feels a need to blink before the movement occurs
